senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. נָדָה) [to keep off,] to vow (abstinence).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 5:1">Ned. V, 1</cite> <he>שנָדְרוּ זה מזה</he> who vowed not to receive benefits from one another.
<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 3:6">Ib. III, 6</cite> <he>הנוֹדֵר מיורדי הים</he> he who vows to forbid himself benefits from seafarers.
<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 6:1">Ib. VI, 1</cite> <he>הנודר מן המבושל</he> who vows to abstain from whatever is cooked.
<cite ref="Nedarim 77b:4">Ib. 77ᵇ</cite> <he>כל הנודר אע״פ וכ׳</he> whoever vows, even if he fulfills his vow, is called a sinner.
<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 1:1">Ib. I, 1</cite> <he>נ׳ בנזיר … ובקרבן</he> his is a valid vow implying nazariteship and sacrifice.
<cite ref="Mishnah Nazir 4:4">Naz. IV, 4</cite> <he>שנָדְרָה בנזיר</he> who vowed to be a Nazarite; a. fr.—Imperative: <cite ref="D00345"><he>דּוֹר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 3:2">Snh. III, 2</cite> <he>דּוֹר לי בחיי ראשך</he> vow (swear) to me by anything concerning thy person (and I will accept it as a legal oath).
<cite ref="Kiddushin 41a:1">Kidd. 41ᵃ</cite> <he>דור הנאה ממנו</he> renounce all benefit from him.—

<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 3:4">Ned. III, 4</cite> <he>נוֹדְרִין להרגין וכ׳</he> (<cite ref="Tosefta Nedarim 2:2">Tosef. ib. II, 2</cite> <he>תולין</he>) you are not bound by a vow made to escape robbery by highway-men &c.

Arakh. I, 1, a. e. נודרים may vow to dedicate the value of a certain person to the sanctuary, contrad. to עָרַךְ q. v.—Part. pass. נָדוּר being under the obligation of a vow; being the legitimate subject of a vow.

<cite ref="Shevuot 20a:14">Shebu. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>והוא שנ׳ ובא מאותו היום</he> provided he was bound by a vow to fast on that day; <cite ref="Nedarim 12a:5">Ned. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>והוא שנ׳ באותו היום</he> (v. Rashi a. l.).
<cite ref="Nedarim 12a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>שנ׳ ובא מאותו היום ואילך</he> that he has vowed to fast regularly on that day (every week).
<cite ref="Nedarim 13a:15">Ib. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>דבר הנ׳</he> a thing which can be made forbidden by a vow (not otherwise forbidden by law).
<cite ref="Nedarim 46a:7">Ib. 46ᵃ</cite> <he>תני ונ׳ הנאה וכ׳</he> interpret <he>מודר</he> as meaning, and he through his own vow is forbidden any benefit &c.
<cite ref="Nazir 9b:1">Naz. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>נ׳ ונזיר</he> he is under the influence of a vow (of abstention from dried figs) and is also a Nazarite; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be made the subject of a vow; to have one’s personal value dedicated to the sanctuary.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 1:1">Arakh. I, 1</cite> <he>נודרים ונִידָּרִים</he> are entitled to dedicate (v. supra) and to be dedicated.
<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 1:3">Ib. 3</cite> <he>לא נ׳</he> cannot be dedicated (has no value); a. fr.
<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 1:10">Meg. I, 10</cite> <he>כל שהוא נִידָּר</he>, v. <cite ref="N00201"><he>נָדַב</he></cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to put a person under the influence of a vow; to prohibit, forbid.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 7:1">Keth. VII, 1</cite> <he>המַדִּיר את אשתו מליהנות לו</he> if one vows that his wife shall derive no benefit from him.

<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 7:1">Ib.</cite> <he>המדיר … שלא תטעום וכ׳</he> if a man (by confirming her vow) subjects his wife to a restriction from tasting &c. Y. ib. 31ᵇ <he>ויש אדם שמדיר את אשתו מחיים</he> (not <he>חבירו</he>) can a man forbid his wife that which belongs to the necessaries of life? Ib. bot. <he>הִדִּירָהּ שלא להשאיל וכ׳</he> if he, by means of a vow, forbade her to lend to her neighbors a winnow or a sieve.
<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 3:3">Ned. III, 3</cite> <he>הִדִּירוֹ חבירו וכ׳</he> if his friend urged him under a vow to dine with him.
Naz. IV, 6 מַדִּיר את בנו בנזיר has power to make his (minor) son a Nazarite; a. fr.—Trnsf. to make inaccessible.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 22a">B. Bath. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>במַדִּיר את כותלו</he>, v. <cite ref="M00325"><he>מָדַר</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: to be forbidden by a vow; to be subjected to the influence of a vow.
units: <cite ref="Gittin 35b:7">Gitt. 35ᵇ</cite> <he>נדר שה׳ ברבים</he> a votary prohibition imposed on a person in public; <cite ref="Gittin 36a:2">ib. 36ᵃ</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 4:1">Ned. IV, 1</cite> <he>המוּדָּר הנאה מחבירו</he> he who is forbidden, by his neighbor’s vow, to derive any benefit &c.
<cite ref="Nedarim 46a:2">Ib. 46ᵃ</cite> <he>היה אחד מהם מודר וכ׳</he> if one was forbidden &c., expl. ‘forbidden through his own vow’, v. supra.
<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 5:4">Ib. V, 4</cite> <he>המודר אסור</he> he against whom the vow was directed is forbidden (all benefits).
<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 1:1">Ib. I, 1</cite> <he>מוּדְּרַנִי ממך</he> I will be (as if) subjected to a vow of thine forbidding me any benefit at thy hands.
Ib. 5ᵃ מודר אני ממך לא משתעינא וכ׳ ‘I will be muddar (kept distant) from thee’ may mean, I will not talk to thee; a. fr.
